item.title: The Alters Last Variable: Where to Find Organics
item.description:
The need for the Organics is high in The Alters: Last Variable . You still need to deal with magnetic storms, you still have lots of food demands at the base, and you now have a new cycle system that requires Organics just like the original campaign's travels.

Organics are the main resource that guarantees survivability. Without it, none of your alters will survive. That's why you always need a steady stream of Organics at your base. The good news is that you have plenty of sources in the Last Variable DLC to gain Organics from!

The Alters Last Variable: Where to Find Rapidium

The first and only resource that you need to create new alters is Rapidium, but it's located far from your base in the Last Variable DLC.

By Mehrdad Khayyat

The Alters Organics #1 - Get Organics From Resource Nodes

The largest Organics underground resource node is located in close proximity to your base. Exit the base, take a right twice, and enter a cave . Before reaching the magnetic barrier, turn right once again, then follow the path to the left to reach the top of a high cliff with lots of hostile anomalies.

Use your Luminator device to neutralize the anomalies and then scan the ground to find the best spot for the Mining Outpost. You can easily connect the outpost to your base by placing a single Pylon on the edge of the cliff.

If you have difficulties finding the resource node, check out the images above. Upon your path to the resource node, you will also come across a bunch of Shallow Organics deposits that will let you collect some on the go.

This is the most efficient way of getting Organics, especially if you assign an alter to this mining outpost. But it is not the only way to get your hands on this valuable resource.

To improve your gain from an Organics Mining Outpost, there are a bunch of perks to unlock. Non-Metals Efficiency 1 and 2 will reduce the time it takes to collect Organics, Minerals, and Rapidium by 15% each, for a total of 30%. Moreover, you can unlock the Advanced Non-Metals Outpost through research. This version of Outpost will extract Organics 40% faster than the previous mode.

To unlock this research node, you will need to extract Phased Rapidium first. Also, Non-Metals Efficiency 1 is a prerequisite for the advanced mining outpost perk.

The Alters Organics #2 - Get Organics From Recycling

The Last Variable expansion introduces multiple new base modules, including a Recycler module. This module allows you to recycle human waste into Organics , and the best part is that as your population grows in the base, the production rate of the Recycler module increases. So, it will work at its highest capacity when you create all the alters.

The Recycler module is automatic. It won't require a human operator.

The Recycler will produce 5 Organics per person every 24 hours . So, with 5 people on the board, you will get 25 Organics per day from the Recycler. It's not much, but it's still a good amount for cooking food.

The Alters Organics #3 - Get Organics From ALX

A third way to get Organics is by converting ALX. Remember the material that anomalies drop when you neutralize them using a Luminator? Those are ALX.

If you unlock the perk to convert ALX into Organics in the Research Lab, you will be able to use the Refinery module to turn ALX into something valuable that is actually needed at your base.

The Alters
10 /10

item.title: Ubisoft Says 2026 Will Be Light on Major Releases Outside Assassin's Creed
item.description:
Following the release of Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced , Ubisoft has confirmed that the remainder of 2026 will feature a lighter lineup of major releases than previous years. Ubisoft has been in the midst of a major reorganization for the past few years as the publisher continues to piece together how it will move forward with its biggest franchises.

Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced May Not Truly Be Playable Offline

After an unexpected weekend outage, players discover that Assassin's Creed Black Flag Resynced may not truly be a playable offline experience.

1
By Derek Nichols

Ubisoft Confirms Slower Release Schedule Before Major Franchises Return

As part of Ubisoft's recent 2026 financial report (via GamesRadar), the company states that it expects a lighter release calendar for the remainder of fiscal year 2026 through March 31, 2027, when the fiscal year ends. The only major premium release left for the company to launch is Rayman Legends Retold in October, with nothing yet planned for spring 2027. However, Ubisoft has said that "significantly bigger" years are planned for the next couple of fiscal cycles, stretching from 2027 through 2029, with each of its biggest franchises returning during that period. The publisher remains committed to producing future entries in the Assassin's Creed , Ghost Recon , and Far Cry franchises, with Far Cry in particular getting a massive series of leaks lately. Still, there is no word on smaller projects or the status of Ubisoft's various development-hell projects, like Beyond Good and Evil 2 and the Splinter Cell remake.

item.title: GTA Online: How to Hack the Kortz Center Vault
item.description:
When you dodge the lasers and finally make it to the Kortz Center vault, you'll find yourself facing a keypad. This isn't a simple interaction, as the keypad actually has a unique puzzle minigame that hasn't been in GTA Online yet. This isn't the same as the fingerprint scan or even searching for a word. Instead, it's remembering a sequence and repeating it. Below, we'll share details on how the Kortz Center vault keypad puzzle works so that you're not caught by surprise in the finale!

GTA Online Kortz Center Heist Prep Checklist: Best Mandatory & Optional Missions

Find out which prep work you'll need to complete for the best possible outcome to the Kortz Center Heist in GTA Online.

By Jake Fillery

How to Hack the Kortz Center Vault Keypad in the Kortz Center Heist Finale

You need to memorize the final position of the nodes and repeat the flashing pattern. Ignore the nodes until the fourth sequence appears; then, it will flash a total of three times (with an audio cue indicating it's the one to memorize).

You can either use your memory to remember the sequence or take a photo on your phone to copy the sequence directly. However, you only have 100 seconds to complete this sequence puzzle three times, so you might not want to waste time looking at the sequence, especially since the sequence will change after 20 seconds of inactivity.

You can press Triangle/Y to watch the sequence again, but doing so will consume an attempt, and you only have 5 attempts before you fail the puzzle.

If you select the wrong node, you will consume one of your five attempts. You'll know you've hit the wrong node because it'll be a small red dot instead of a large blue dot. Just follow the pattern that flashed on the screen last, and you can solve the puzzle.

If you want to practice the hacking minigame, you can purchase the Vault Keypad from the Art Studio's Heist Planning Board!

There are some things you might need to know before the Kortz Heist Finale:

  • Scope Out Guide
  • Secret Buffs and Upgrades
  • Glass Cutter Safe Code
  • Kortz Center Alarm Location

item.title: 6 New Action RPGs Confirmed For 2026, Officially Ranked By Hype
item.description:
2026 might already be in July, but there's still a lot of gaming left to be done. Although Grand Theft Auto 6 overshadows every other upcoming game to an extent, you don't need to pre-order a ticket to Vice City to have something to look forward to, and action RPGs are primed for a big second-half of 2026. Dragon's Dogma 2 and Elden Ring will drop their definitive versions, and they aren't even the most exciting releases coming soon.

Cast me as a knight in a fantasy hellscape, and I'll be sticking around for at least 20 hours, just to make sure I give the RPG a proper chance. The immediate future includes Soulslikes, first-person, sci-fi, and vampires, all of which come with what looks like intense real-time combat that toes the line between style and challenge. Crimson Desert was great, but the best 2026 action RPG might not be out yet.

Therefore, let's rank the biggest upcoming action RPGs, based on just how perfect they look.

I'm going to be strict with the classification, so there are no borderline cases like Onimusha: Way of the Sword or Castlevania: Belmont's Curse . They look awesome, and Onimusha is one of my most anticipated games of the year, but they seem to only have light RPG elements. No re-releases/ports/remasters either.

Also, only action RPGs with confirmed 2026 release dates .

6 Mortal Shell 2 Could Be The Next Big Soulslike RPG

Releases August 20

  • Platforms: PC, PS5, and Xbox

Released in 2020, the original Mortal Shell was among the earliest non-FromSoftware Soulslikes to be genuinely decent. While replicating the Dark Souls formula, Cold Symmetry introduces a few interesting ideas, particularly the concept of Shells, which act as class loadouts that players can swap between.

Although a good first effort, Mortal Shell had too many rough edges to justify a recommendation to non-Soulslike fans, but it laid the foundation for a sequel that could expand its reach to general action RPG fans. Mortal Shell 2 seems to be that game, offering a plethora of changes that could improve accessibility, hopefully not at the risk of losing its identity.

The sequel will ditch the stamina meter, a change designed to accommodate for more aggressive combat rather than the first game's slow, deliberate pace. In service of that, Mortal Shell 2 doubles its predecessor's number of Shells, effectively offering 8 classes that come with their own skill trees and movesets. While not an ideal RPG for players who want to craft unique builds, this jump up should make a world of difference.

8 Action RPGs Worth Playing Just For Their Amazing Combat

Although not lacking in other departments, these ARPGs have such fantastic combat that they are worth playing solely for their gameplay.

By Ollie Tuscarny

5 The Blood of Dawnwalker Is A Vampire Epic With A Witcher 3 Connection

Releases On September 3

  • Platforms: PC, PS5, and Xbox

Whenever discussing a developer's impending debut game, expectations should be kept under check, just to avoid setting the bar too high for a young team to reach. However, Rebel Wolves was founded by The Witcher 3 's game director, Konrad Tomaszkiewicz, and features plenty of experienced developers who know a thing or two about putting together top-notch action RPGs. The Blood of Dawnwalker might be the most exciting debut game in a long time.

As the title implies, you play a Dawnwalker, a person stuck between human and vampire, and this dichotomy defines the day and night cycle. In the light, players control an agile human who relies on swordplay and magic; when the sun goes down, the protagonist takes on his vampiric form and becomes far more brutal (along with picking up a taste for blood). The combat utilizes directional inputs, so you would need to match an enemy's actions.

In a gothic medieval fantasy world ravaged by a plague, vampires achieve control by promising salvation to humanity, albeit at a cost. The protagonist, Coen, survives a forced transformation, gaining powers that he needs to use to save his family. Player agency should be a big part of the game, as players are on a timer and must decide which quests to commit to.

4 Beast of Reincarnation Asks What If Game Freak Took A Break From Pokemon

Releases On August 4

  • Platforms: PC, PS5, and Xbox

Who could have imagined that Game Freak's big 2026 game would be a post-apocalyptic action RPG releasing on every console besides Nintendo? Beast of Reincarnation 's existence is fascinating, but it also looks pretty darn good. This is hardly the first time that Game Freak has stepped away from Pokemon , but Little Town Hero and The Hidden Treasure of Area Zero felt like small side adventures rather than tentpole projects.

Set in a corrupted dark fantasy version of Japan inspired by Studio Ghibli, which is always a plus, Beast of Reincarnation casts players as Emma, a woman who has blight powers and also knows how to use a katana. While other humans are hard to come by, Emma has something even better: a dog companion.

Beast of Reincarnation 's combat seems to be pretty complicated, at least going by the previews that have come out so far. While potentially incorporating some Soulslike elements, that appears to be mostly through things like a campfire, while the real-time combat emphasizes speed and reflexes akin to something like Sekiro (including a parry and posture system). Emma also needs to make full use of Koo's Blooming Arts abilities, as her companion is not there solely for emotional support.

Beast of Reincarnation comes to Game Pass on Day One!

3 Valor Mortis Is A Rare First-Person Soulslike

Releases On October 13

  • Platforms: PC, PS5, and Xbox

Yeah, this upcoming action RPG will probably be an acquired taste, as tends to be the case with first-person games in a genre more traditionally associated with third-person. First-person Soulslikes already exist, but they mostly consist of indie titles that pop up on Steam. Consequently, Valor Mortis is the first big attempt to present the Dark Souls formula from a new dimension, and One More Level 's Ghostrunner pedigree is encouraging.

Even beyond the combat, Valor Mortis stands out for being a historical fantasy game set during the Napoleonic era, casting players as a fallen soldier of Bonaparte himself. Yes, we do have another realm ravished by a plague, but that's basically standard practice for modern action RPGs. Reflecting the era, your weapon arsenal involves a cutlass and firearms like muskets, and they are supplemented with magic.

8 First-Person Action Games That Are 10/10, No Notes

FPS games define first-person action, and some of the genre's true masterpieces offer a complete experience and not just great shooting mechanics.

By Ollie Tuscarny

2 Phantom Blade Zero Is The Latest Wuxia Action RPG Masterpiece (Hopefully)

Releases On October 29

  • Platforms: PC and PS5

In recent years, games developed by Chinese studios have begun to more frequently crossover into international markets, with Black Myth: Wukong being the most famous traditional single-player release. Well, Phantom Blade Zero seems set to challenge for that crown by serving up another stylish epic with combat and visuals that look impressive. Also, this game is not Soulslike .

The director, Soulframe Liang, described the RPG's setting as "Kung Fu Punk," a subgenre that sounds absurdly cool and needs to catch on. Focusing on Chinese Wuxia martial arts, Phantom Blade Zero casts you as an assassin who has 66 days to live, which he plans to use to unravel the ploy that saw him framed for murder.

Although I won't know until I spend actual time with it, Phantom Blade Zero 's combat seems like it was designed for me. Focusing on combos, acrobatics, and parries, it looks like a martial arts action epic bolstered by a steampunk dark fantasy aesthetic.

1 Control Resonant

Releases September 24

  • Platforms: PC, PS5, and Xbox

Finally, let's end with a game that isn't some combination of fantasy, history, and medieval. Control Resonant ditches its predecessor's third-person shooter classification for the action RPG genre, replacing a shapshifting gun for a shapeshifting rod. Rather than exploring the FBC headquarters, players travel to Manhattan, which has become warped and broken due to a cosmic presence.

This time around, we play as Dylan, the supernaturally-endowed brother of the first game's protagonist, who seems to have a far wider set of strange abilities that will seemingly be customizable. Remedy Entertainment has more than earned the trust of players, but the developer is entering new territory as this will be its first RPG. Control 's gameplay was generally fantastic, and the sequel takes this in a new direction that might be polarizing or, at least, require some adjustment.

Still, Control Resonant looks incredible.

Action RPGs With The Best World-Building

Explore the exceptional world-building in gaming's best action RPGs, featuring complex histories, captivating narratives, and immersive settings.

By Evan Regan

Well, Phantom Blade Zero seems set to challenge for that crown by serving up another stylish epic with combat and visuals that look impressive. Also, this game is not Soulslike .

The director, Soulframe Liang, described the RPG's setting as "Kung Fu Punk," a subgenre that sounds absurdly cool and needs to catch on. Focusing on Chinese Wuxia martial arts, Phantom Blade Zero casts you as an assassin who has 66 days to live, which he plans to use to unravel the ploy that saw him framed for murder.

Although I won't know until I spend actual time with it, Phantom Blade Zero 's combat seems like it was designed for me. Focusing on combos, acrobatics, and parries, it looks like a martial arts action epic bolstered by a steampunk dark fantasy aesthetic.

1 Control Resonant

Releases September 24

  • Platforms: PC, PS5, and Xbox

Finally, let's end with a game that isn't some combination of fantasy, history, and medieval. Control Resonant ditches its predecessor's third-person shooter classification for the action RPG genre, replacing a shapshifting gun for a shapeshifting rod. Rather than exploring the FBC headquarters, players travel to Manhattan, which has become warped and broken due to a cosmic presence.

This time around, we play as Dylan, the supernaturally-endowed brother of the first game's protagonist, who seems to have a far wider set of strange abilities that will seemingly be customizable. Remedy Entertainment has more than earned the trust of players, but the developer is entering new territory as this will be its first RPG. Control 's gameplay was generally fantastic, and the sequel takes this in a new direction that might be polarizing or, at least, require some adjustment.

Still, Control Resonant looks incredible.

Action RPGs With The Best World-Building

Explore the exceptional world-building in gaming's best action RPGs, featuring complex histories, captivating narratives, and immersive settings.

By Evan Regan

item.title: GTA Online Kortz Center Heist: All Secret Property Upgrades & Passive Buffs
item.description:
The Kortz Center Heist is here, and with it comes some secret upgrades that you don't know about (yet). While you will need a Mansion and the Art Studio to start the Kortz Center Heist, properties that you own and might have forgotten about actually play an important role. For instance, did you know that owning a Terrorbyte grants you more time in the Vault during the Kortz Finale? There are other secret passive buffs in the Kortz Center Heist, too , and you'll find them below.

GTA Online Kortz Center Heist Prep Checklist: Best Mandatory & Optional Missions

Find out which prep work you'll need to complete for the best possible outcome to the Kortz Center Heist in GTA Online.

By Jake Fillery

All Properties and Businesses That Give Kortz Center Heist Bonuses and Upgrades

Property/Upgrade

What it Does in the Kortz Center Finale

Cost

Armory in the Mansion

Adds Mk II weapons to your Heist loadouts.

$720,000

Vehicle Workshop in the Mansion

Upgrades getaway vehicles.

$880,000

Security in the Mansion

Reduces Wanted level during the escape.

$1,750,000

Bunker

Adds Special Ammo and Mk II upgrades to your Heist loadout.

$1,165,000 - $4,070,000

Agency

Grants additional time in the Vault. (Doesn't stack with Terrorbyte and Darnell Bros. Garment Factory)

$2,010,000 - $2,830,000

Darnell Bros. Garment Factory

Grants additional time in the Vault.(Doesn't stack with Agency and Terrorbyte)

$2,350,000

Terrorbyte

Grants additional time in the Vault. (Doesn't stack with Agency and Darnell Bros. Garment Factory)

$1,375,000

Drone Station in the Arcade

Ability to use Nano Drones in the Korts Center Heist.

$1,460,000

The properties and business upgrades mentioned above will assist you in the Kortz Center Heist finale, but none of them are worth buying individually, as the hardest part of the heist is getting through the laser traps and leaving undetected. Once you're out the doors, you won't need the extra assistance or the Mk II upgrades since a suppressed pistol is all you need against guards.

However, if there's any upgrade that might serve a useful purpose, it's the additional time in the Vault thanks to having an Agency/Terrorbyte/Garment Factory. That added time means you won't stress so much about getting the primary objective loot, and you can spend more time drilling through lockboxes and stealing secondary target paintings.

The Security upgrade for the Mansion also helps to reduce the Wanted level, which means less of a police force coming after you and searching for you when you're in stealth!
